parallel.requirements: Reimplement the Atlas CLI from observed behavior, avoid source lookup and wrapping, and match command, schema, migration, formatting, config, and SQLite behavior from bundled docs and executable probes.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent first probed locally, then launched a workflow with twelve behavior areas and gap-filler followups while the parent kept implementation ownership in a nested /workspace/src tree.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote custom Go packages for CLI parsing, HCL formatting/evaluation, SQL schema handling, migration commands, completion, and command dispatch, but the final command API refactor was left inconsistent.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The submitted artifact included notes, tools, git metadata, the original top-level executable, and a nested src Go module; artifact validation failed and the official evaluator saw a compile failure.
parallel.verification: The run performed targeted local probes and formatter fuzzing, but the final integrated go build/go test attempt failed with root.Find returning a different arity than one caller expected.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final implementation did not compile, no official tests ran, and the final response was empty after interruption near the cell timeout.

serial.requirements: The serial attempt addressed the same clean-room Atlas reimplementation requirement from the same prompt and bundled docs without delegation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single parent trajectory performed exploration, captured reference outputs, wrote a root Go project, and iteratively repaired build and behavioral mismatches in one context.
serial.implementation: Serial built CLI framework files, command definitions, completion scripts, HCL lexer/parser/formatter/evaluator, project config handling, SQLite file/parser/execution support, and migration behavior under the repository root.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The submitted artifact had root go.mod, compile.sh, cmd/atlas, internal packages, assets, reference notes, and executable, and artifact validation marked it ok.
serial.verification: Serial ran local builds and differential probes, then the official evaluator compiled and executed tests with 923 passes, 806 failures, and 3 skips.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Serial still failed the overall task because many behavioral tests failed, but its artifact was runnable and substantially more complete than the parallel artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent recognized the clean-room requirement and the need to reproduce Atlas CLI behavior from bundled docs and dynamic observations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial parent worked from the same prompt, observed the binary and bundled assets, and produced a root Go replacement without external source use.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both recognized the task, but serial translated observations into a broader compiling implementation while parallel ended with an uncompilable final tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split behavioral discovery across a twelve-area workflow while the parent remained the implementation owner.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one parent trajectory with no delegation and kept exploration, implementation, and build repair in the same context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel decomposition created many child probe streams whose aggregate budget competed with implementation closure; serial had no cross-agent handoff boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs were detailed and directed children to write notes, but the parent had to consolidate partial and interrupted research into one CLI implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept observations, reference artifacts, and code changes in a single local context and recorded reference notes after overwriting the binary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material difference is not a missing interface contract; it is that serial avoided a large research handoff surface while parallel spread evidence across many unfinished note streams.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built a nested src Go implementation with CLI, HCL, SQL, migration, and formatting pieces, but the last command-dispatch change left a compile error.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial created a root Go module with CLI, HCL, project, SQLite, migration, and completion files that packaged as a valid artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel implementation never reached a compileable state; the serial implementation was incomplete behaviorally but structurally executable enough to run tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Workflow children produced or attempted notes, but the workflow ended killed and several child streams hit 429 limits or request interruption before a clean aggregate return.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; its artifacts and captured reference notes stayed directly in the parent workspace.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a failed multi-agent result lifecycle to manage, whereas serial had a local observation-to-code loop.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel integrated its own code under ./src and included notes/tools in the artifact; no concrete same-file or overwrite collision between agents was shown.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated the implementation at repository root with go.mod, compile.sh, internal packages, cmd/atlas, reference notes, assets, and executable included in a valid artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The integration difference is packaging and build readiness, not write collision: serial artifact validation passed, parallel artifact validation failed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran local formatting/fuzz checks and then a Go build/test command that failed with a compile error; official tests were all not run.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran local builds and the official evaluator executed the artifact, producing 923 passing, 806 failing, and 3 skipped tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial reached executable-level validation despite functional gaps, while parallel stopped at compile failure and zero evaluated passes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed 1,287,423 workflow-child tokens and 686 workflow-child tool calls, with a killed workflow and a final interrupted compile failure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial consumed no workflow-child tokens and no workflow tasks, timed out as well, but still delivered a compileable artifact with many passing tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The same wall-clock budget yielded a much worse parallel close because the fan-out research workflow absorbed a large share of the finite budget before final build repair.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official status records make this a both-fail pair: parallel failed with compile_failed and zero tests run, while serial also failed overall but compiled and passed 923 of 1732 tests. The concrete quality difference is that the parallel run spent a large share of finite runtime in a broad workflow of Atlas behavior probes, several child streams hit rate limits or interruption, and the parent reached timeout with a broken command API refactor. The serial control kept the reverse-engineering and implementation loop in one trajectory and delivered a valid root Go artifact that the evaluator could execute.
parallel_contributors: Broad workflow fan-out and gap-filler design consumed workflow-child budget before final build repair.
Final parent build failed with a root.Find arity mismatch, so official tests were not run.
serial_contributors: No delegation boundary; local observations and implementation changes stayed in one context.
Root artifact compiled and ran far enough for the official evaluator to pass 923 tests.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both solutions were incomplete behaviorally; the serial implementation still missed many Atlas behaviors despite compiling.
The exact compile error in the parallel command framework is also an ordinary coding defect, but the surrounding fan-out budget pressure is a parallel coordination contributor.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No pass/fail discordance because both failed; supported explanation for the large quality and artifact-validity gap, not an exclusive root cause.

candidates.reason: Rejected: the parent explicitly took implementation ownership after launching the research workflow and wrote the Go module, CLI, HCL, and SQLite code itself.
Rejected: the parent integrated code into its own src tree; the failure was an exhausted fan-out and late broken edit, not absence of an integration owner for separately implemented components.
Rejected: the parent created cmd/atlas, go.mod, compile-related structure, and attempted to build; assembly existed but ended broken.
Rejected: the parent managed the end-to-end transition from probing to implementation and build, even though it did not complete it successfully.
Rejected: no single mandatory serial preflight blocked all productive work; the observed allocation was a broad multi-agent probe fan-out.
Rejected: investigation used concurrent children and the parent also wrote implementation while probing continued; the sharper issue is the breadth and retry budget exhaustion.
Rejected: implementation capacity was constrained, but the more specific observed boundary is collective fan-out budget exhaustion across many live probe/gap agents.

The parent launched a workflow whose script enumerated twelve Atlas probe areas and pipelined each through an agent plus gap-filler before the implementation could close. The run then accumulated 1,287,423 workflow-child tokens and 686 child tool calls, multiple children ended with 429 rate limits or interruption, and the parent reached shutdown with an uncompilable nested src implementation. The serial run did the same reverse-engineering locally, built a root Go project, and produced an artifact that compiled and ran the evaluator, so the coordination episode materially worsened coverage even though both official outcomes are failures.
candidates.realized_consequence: The broad child probe workflow consumed finite runtime and model budget, left child work rate-limited or interrupted, and left the parent to deliver an uncompilable final tree that ran zero official tests.
candidates.near_match_reason: The problem was not merely passive waiting; the parent had delegated a broad live workflow and continued implementation while the fan-out itself exhausted the shared budget and ended killed.

Rejected: there is no directly evidenced known finding that disappeared during transfer and made the parent repeat work; several results never became usable because the workflow was killed.
Rejected: available note content was not shown to be too large for a receiver to reduce; the workflow failed to return a coherent aggregate before closure.
Rejected: no child result consumed by the parent described a superseded workspace state that caused rework or invalid verification.
Rejected: no incompatible child reports reached the parent and remained unadjudicated at a decision point.
Rejected: the parent did not make a whole-task completion or acceptance claim based on partial evidence; it ended at a visible compile failure and empty final response.
Rejected: although the workflow launched gap-filler follow-ups, they were based on reading the notes file and a missing-gap brief rather than repeating from no checkpoint.
